title: Half-knot stitch
subtitle: A single-wrap knot used for dots smaller than a French knot.
excerpt: A half-knot stitch is a single wrap around the needle before re-entry. It produces a smaller, flatter knot than the French knot and works well for fine detail at a small scale.
sourceNotes:
Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), Project Gutenberg #20776. Knot stitch variations.
Caulfeild and Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882), Internet Archive. Knot stitch entries.

glossaryTerms.definition: A single-wrap knot stitch: the thread wraps once around the needle before it re-enters the cloth, creating a small flat knot on the surface, smaller than a French knot.

content.text: is formed with a single wrap around the needle rather than the two wraps of a French knot. The result is a flatter, smaller knot on the surface. It is the better choice for fine detail work where a French knot would overwhelm the surrounding stitches.

items.name: Stranded cotton, 1 strand for fine work

content.text: Anchor the thread and bring the needle up at the knot position.
Hold the thread with the non-needle hand about 3 cm from the cloth.
Wrap the thread once around the needle.
Push the needle back into the cloth one thread away from where it emerged.
Hold the thread taut with the left hand while drawing the needle fully through the cloth with the right.

items.symptom: The knot looks the same as a French knot
items.cause: Two wraps were used instead of one.
items.fix: One wrap only. Practise on a spare piece of cloth until one and two wraps feel distinct.

items.symptom: The knot disappears to the back
items.cause: The needle went back through the same hole it emerged from.
items.fix: Re-enter one thread away from the emergence hole.

content.text: Half-knot stitches are used in miniature work and in blackwork where French knots would read too heavy. The
also forms the basis of the bullion knot, where multiple wraps produce an elongated cylindrical knot.
